standards: engage in different types of language learning activities;
compare and contrast aspects of other languages to English and the student's native language; and
apply basic communication skills in the target language(s), including listening, speaking, reading, and writing.
identify and describe cultural practices in selected regions or countries;
recognize the cultural products such as art, music, food, clothing, or other culturally related examples in selected regions or countries; and
compare and contrast aspects of other cultures to the student's own culture.
engage in a variety of language learning strategies such as identifying cognates and recognizing word origins; and
demonstrate an awareness of language patterns such as word/character order, grammatical structures, and symbols.
introduce self and others using basic, culturally-appropriate greetings;
ask simple questions and provide simple responses related to personal preferences; and
exchange essential information about self, family, and familiar topics.
identify and describe selected cultural practices and perspectives such as traditions, daily life, and celebrations;
examine significant historic and contemporary influences from the cultures studied such as explorers, artists, musicians, and athletes; and
describe various products across cultures such as food, shelter, clothing, transportation, sports and recreation, music, art, and dance.

use authentic materials such as maps, graphs, graphic organizers, and other print and visual materials or literature to reinforce comprehension and expression of basic vocabulary in the target language; and
research and present information on historical and contemporary cultural influences.
compare and contrast selected cultural practices and perspectives such as traditions, daily life, and celebrations to student's own culture;
give examples of cognates, false cognates, idiomatic expressions, or sentence structure to show understanding of how languages are alike and different; and
demonstrate how media such as television, Internet, newspapers, and advertisements represent selected cultural similarities and differences.
participate in cultural events in local, global, or online communities and discuss experiences and perspectives gained;
research careers in which cross-cultural awareness or LOTE language skills are needed; and
describe how cultural awareness impacts personal growth.
engage in a variety of ASL exchanges of learned material to socialize and to provide and obtain information;
demonstrate an understanding of basic ASL such as simple stories, everyday commands, and brief instructions when dealing with familiar topics;
convey information in ASL using familiar words, concepts, classifiers, phrases, and sentences to others without voice;
demonstrate appropriate usage of ASL phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and pragmatics; and
be exposed to and experience ASL literature such as handshape stories that follows traditional cultural features.
recognize and use Deaf cultural norms to demonstrate an understanding of the perspectives of American Deaf culture;
show evidence of appreciation of ASL literature created by the Deaf and how it applies to the perspectives of American Deaf culture;

show evidence of appreciation of the contributions by the Deaf and how they are applied to the perspectives of American Deaf culture such as historical, geographical, political, artistic, and scientific avenues; and
demonstrate an understanding of Deaf history and how it applies to the perspectives of American Deaf culture.
use resources and digital technology to gain access to information about ASL and Deaf culture; and
use ASL to obtain, reinforce, or expand knowledge of other subject areas.
demonstrate an understanding of the nature of language through comparisons of the student's own language and ASL;
demonstrate an understanding of the nature of culture through comparisons of the student's own culture and the American Deaf culture; and
demonstrate an understanding of how one language and culture can influence another.
apply ASL at the novice proficiency level in or out of the school setting through involvement in cultural activities such as attending Deaf events;
be aware of methods of technology to communicate with the Deaf/ASL community; and
show evidence of becoming a lifelong learner by using ASL at the novice proficiency level for personal enrichment and/or career development.
